metadata.title: Short sellers are coming after SpaceX as it sheds post-IPO gains

content.text:
Scott Melker discusses the trading volatility and short activity around SpaceX (SPCX) — the Elon Musk-led company's stock shedding its post-IPO gains — especially as it issues its first debt sale since going public.
"The Daily Wolf with Scott Melker" airs every day at 12:00 p.m. Tune in for your daily dose of all things crypto.
Make sure to also check out Yahoo Finance's new crypto hub to find the latest crypto-related news.
SpaceX. Now, I want to preface this by saying we spent so much time in this world, uh building a green planet and on conservation and I never thought that I would live to see the day that trillionaires would become extinct.
RIP trillionaires. Yeah, obviously, it was a huge story for about five minutes that Elon Musk had become a trillionaire on paper and, you know, if he colonized Mars and put data centers in space. But let's not get let facts get in the way of reality.
The guy was no richer the day SpaceX launched than he was the day before. Same amount of money in his bank account. But the story here is obviously the massive pump and dump in price action that we saw on SpaceX.
Actually, we brought up the chart. It's really interesting.
Can I do that? I didn't do it. Uh, but you can see there obviously, we had that move up to $225 or so and then, uh, have had it hitting a low yesterday, $147, you know, trading around the 150s today.
But this was the most telegraphed, predictable pump and dump situation in history.
Now, I had the 'how not to invest' where I showed you somebody who had gone all in with their retirement fund at $210 and said, that's going to go really badly. Well, there's a reason it was going really badly because for the first four days, there were no sellers.
Literally anyone who wanted SpaceX had to buy it on the market because early investors are locked. There was no way to short it, there were no sellers, no options. And then, of course, predictably, we had options launch on June 16th and it's been nothing but down since.
Why? Because then people could actually short into the retail interest for this thing and it has crashed massively. Tale as old as time, low float, uh options are launched and all of a sudden people can short and price goes down.
Now, Bitcoin enthusiasts may remember December 17th of 2017 when we cheered at the top of the bull market to the day that we were getting Bitcoin futures on CBOE and then later on CME.
That was the dead top of the Bitcoin cycle for years. To the day was the day that institutions can come in and say, this thing is stupid, it's overvalued, we're going to short it.
That is exactly what has happened here with SpaceX. Now, there's another thread very briefly to this uh SpaceX story, which is this and is being viewed as part of the reason it's down.
SpaceX raises 25 billion in debt sale less than two weeks after IPO.
So they had a 100 billion in cash and ran off to the gas station with their full tank of gas and was like, yeah, pump some more in there, baby. Right? Raising 25 billion. So listen, there's 90 billion were offered.
So they got almost 4x what they were asking, but the market didn't like that they were rushing to the market for cash so soon after the IPO. Why is this interesting? Because I told you a story yesterday about Robinhood and their convertible note, and of course, we talked about Alphabet and their preferred and convertible note, and it all ties into the strategy, no pun intended, that has been championed by Strategy.
So we have this interesting situation. We've got a massive sell off but a heavy thirst for this debt, but the narrative around the debt is sending the price of the asset much lower.
